channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Mineral-integrated electrochemical system enabling membrane-free pH swing and active chlorine species generation for urine valorization
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77732-5

A membrane‑free electrochemical alkalization and electrooxidation system for urine valorization enables efficient phosphorus recovery and urea stabilization, providing a scalable route for nutrient recycling and sustainable fertilizer production.
item.dc:title: Mineral-integrated electrochemical system enabling membrane-free pH swing and active chlorine species generation for urine valorization

item.title: RICTOR regulates an interspecies crosstalk that influences longevity through a methionine cycle-mitophagy axis
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77722-7

Physiological traits are modulated in response to diet. Here the authors show that RICTOR restrains host responses to vitamin B12 in C. elegans by modulating organellar quality control and regulating lifespan.
item.dc:title: RICTOR regulates an interspecies crosstalk that influences longevity through a methionine cycle-mitophagy axis

item.title: Built-in electric field-boosted attomolar Pb²⁺ sensing on carboxylated black phosphorene
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77793-6

Lead ion (Pb²⁺) contamination remains a threat to environmental safety and human health, requiring sensitive detectors. Here, the authors report the realization of carboxyl-functionalized black phosphorene modified surface plasmon resonance sensors with detection limit down to 10⁻¹⁹ M and good selectivity against other metal ions.
item.dc:title: Built-in electric field-boosted attomolar Pb²⁺ sensing on carboxylated black phosphorene

item.title: Telomere length of both parents contributes to heritable POT1 cancer-predisposition syndrome
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77414-2

Using haplotype-specific nanopore sequencing, the authors show that cancer-associated POT1 mutations reshape telomere inheritance across generations through germline and post-fertilization remodeling of the shortest telomeres.
item.dc:title: Telomere length of both parents contributes to heritable POT1 cancer-predisposition syndrome

item.title: Metamaterial-enabled battery-free wireless sensor networks for unencumbered human-machine interactions
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77600-2

A battery-free wireless body sensor network enabled by metamaterial textiles is reported. Using a smartphone as a hub, it wirelessly powers distributed sensors for unencumbered human-machine interactions in robotics, VR, and digital twins.
item.dc:title: Metamaterial-enabled battery-free wireless sensor networks for unencumbered human-machine interactions

item.title: Studying the failure mechanism in Li-metal electrode by a reversible fluorescence analysis methodology
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77648-0

Understanding Li electrode failure is challenged by efficient evaluation of solid electrolyte interphase. Here, authors develop a qualitative and quantitative fluorescent method to correlate solid byproducts and accumulated dead Li in the solid electrolyte interphase, identifying the underlying role of side reactions.
item.dc:title: Studying the failure mechanism in Li-metal electrode by a reversible fluorescence analysis methodology

item.title: Angiotensin II exacerbates intracerebral hemorrhage in mice via heparin-like antithrombin activation and coagulation dysfunction
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77481-5

Here, the authors show that angiotensin II acts as a key coagulation regulator with heparin-like antithrombin activation function in mediating hemorrhage. Targeting the angiotensin II coagulation pathway could be a novel strategy to mitigate cerebral bleeding events.
item.dc:title: Angiotensin II exacerbates intracerebral hemorrhage in mice via heparin-like antithrombin activation and coagulation dysfunction

item.title: Tackling chlorine poisoning for robust upcycling of PVC-contaminated plastic streams
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77736-1

Chlorine released from mixed plastic waste can deactivate catalysts and hinder recycling. Here, the authors report a room-temperature treatment to clean ruthenium surfaces, restoring highly active and reusable catalysts for plastic upcycling.
item.dc:title: Tackling chlorine poisoning for robust upcycling of PVC-contaminated plastic streams
